thread:
alex: Quick follow-up: I want to propose a "graceful fallback" metadata field in rollout manifests so clients can prefer prior variants when a rollout shows instability, instead of failing or immediately rolling back. Open to pushback.

maria: Clarify: is this a client-only hint (SDK) or do we expect routing to honor it server-side?

alex: Start client-side. SDKs get a structured hint and make a probabilistic/sticky decision. Server-side routing hooks are possible later but we shouldn't block on that.

jordan: What does the schema look like? Need to avoid open free-form fields that ops misuse.

alex: Draft block: `graceful_fallback:{window_s:300,initial_weight:0.75,min_weight:0.2,decay:"exp",signal:"latency_spike",sticky_s:60}`. Weight is interpreted by SDK as probability to use fallback on new sessions.

sam: Two operational concerns: 1) client-side probability could create uneven load distribution -> autoscaler churn. 2) clients toggling per-request will be chaotic. We need sticky decisions and rate caps.

maria: Agreed. Add `sticky_s` default 60s and recommend SDKs cache a decision per user/session. Also add `max_fallbacks_per_minute` telemetry cap.

jordan: Let's enumerate signals: enum("latency_spike","error_rate","quality_regression","manual_flag"). Don't accept arbitrary strings for signal. If ops need extra context, provide `signal_hint` opaque string for UI only.

alex: Also include `schema_version` at rollout top-level so older clients ignore unknown blocks. We'll make graceful_fallback optional and only honored by schema_version >=2.

sam: Telemetry: emit `rollout.graceful_fallback_chosen` event when an SDK decides fallback. Fields: from_variant, to_variant, reason_signal, decision_weight, sticky_until. That will let us detect abuse.

maria: Console controls: gate who can enable graceful_fallback (rollout owners + SRE), require justification field, and create an audit entry. Add a small chart that overlays fallback weight vs latency/error metrics.

jordan: Backcompat: default behavior for clients that don't understand the field should be to ignore it. Make that explicit in API docs.

alex: For header support, servers can emit `x-rw-rollout: fallback=latency_spike;w=0.75;sticky=60` so non-SDK customers can implement behavior. Document that headers are advisory only.

sam: SDK tests: unit tests for weight math (with decays), sticky behavior, and rate caps. Also integration test to ensure that when fallback is active we log telemetry and do not exceed `max_fallbacks_per_minute`.

maria: UX: allow ops to simulate client decisions in console (toggle simulate=true) to preview effect on traffic. Also warn if autopilot detectors (autoscaler) might be impacted.

jordan: Edge case: pinned variants must never be overridden by fallback. Explicit rule: pins take precedence, graceful_fallback applies only to dynamic routing / unpinned traffic.

alex: Implementation plan: 1) RFC patch with schema example + enums + telemetry events. 2) SDK change: read hint, make sticky probabilistic decision, emit telemetry. 3) Console: gating + audit + simulation. 4) Optional server routing hooks if we see adoption.

sam: One more: decay math preference. Exponential decay from initial_weight -> min_weight over window_s seems safest. Provide readable formula in RFC.

maria: I'll draft the console mockups and permission matrix.

jordan: I'll review the RFC and the header semantics. Also add a note about security: headers must not be trusted for auth or accounting.

sre-bot: Reminder: enable rollout alarms when this is enabled so SRE can be paged if metric regressions happen.

alex: Thanks everyone. I'll file the RFC diff with examples and link it here for review.
